Formula: Fundamental Theorem of Calculus (Part 2)
Exact Expression: \int_{a}^{b} f(x) \, dx = F(b) - F(a)
Definitions: Connects differentiation and definite integration, proving that definite integrals can be computed using antiderivatives.
Derivation/Reference: Isaac Barrow, James Gregory, Isaac Newton, Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz (1670-1684)
Example: int_0^2 (3x^2) dx = [x^3]_0^2 = 2^3 - 0^3 = 8
Domain: calculus
Assumptions: f is continuous on closed interval [a, b]; F'(x) = f(x) for all x in (a, b)
Common Errors: Applying FTC to integrand with jump or asymptotic discontinuity inside [a, b]
subject: Fundamental Theorem of Calculus (Part 2)
